currentContext.strategies: Plastic waste is collected in line with the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) plan submitted to the Pollution Control Board, and the Company completed its EPR targets for the reporting period with the help of a third-party recycler.|Waste oil generated at restaurants is disposed through designated vendors for production of bio-diesel and other approved by-products.|E-waste from restaurant operations, corporate offices and IT infrastructure is disposed through authorised recyclers and vendors in compliance with e-waste management regulations, and paper waste is disposed safely through municipal waste collection.|Food safety and quality assurance framework is being strengthened through enhanced testing protocols, regular vendor compliance assessments, employee training and certification programmes, periodic audits and facility inspections, alongside consumer awareness initiatives across digital and in-store platforms.|Customer data protection commitment: the Company does not retain sensitive customer financial details such as full card numbers, CVV information or card expiry dates.|Workforce diversity: women constitute 36.40% of the total employee base of 12,372 as at March 31, 2026 (37.29% of permanent employees).|Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for communities, investors, shareholders, employees (whistleblower@rbrandsasia.com), customers and value chain partners.|BRSR reporting boundary is standalone and no external assurance provider has been appointed (type of assurance obtained: Not Applicable).
currentContext.expansion: RBA's expansion is asset-light restaurant-footprint growth rather than plant capex. In FY 2026 the India business added 68 net restaurants, taking the network to 581 Burger King outlets as of March 31, 2026 (including 5 sub-franchisee restaurants), of which 559 restaurants include BK Cafes that add a coffee and expanded-menu format to the existing box. The Company retains exclusive master franchise rights to develop, establish, operate and franchise Burger King restaurants in India, and through its Indonesian subsidiaries to develop Burger King and Popeyes in Indonesia, so future expansion runs through new restaurant development under a well-defined roll-out and development process supported by a vertically managed, scalable supply chain. On the funding side, the Company raised Rs 500 Crores through a Qualified Institutions Placement on March 26, 2025 with no deviation in the use of proceeds from the stated objects as on March 31, 2026, and enlarged its authorised share capital twice during the year - from Rs 600 crore to Rs 700 crore (AGM, August 21, 2025) and then to Rs 900 crore (EGM, February 13, 2026) - creating headroom for further issuance. Separately, Lenexis Foodworks Private Limited (Inspira Global's food and beverage arm) is to acquire a controlling stake together with a significant capital infusion aimed at supporting long-term growth in the QSR segment, subject to regulatory approvals. No rupee capex budget, new-store target or dated commissioning schedule is disclosed in the routed text.

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR as a material risk: safety issues arising from contamination of food in dine-in restaurants or in food delivered for at-home consumption can lead to severe reputational risk. Failure to maintain standards may result in increased compliance costs, business interruptions, customer complaints, regulatory scrutiny and reputational harm that could adversely affect sales and long-term brand equity. Mitigated through SOPs compliant with local regulations, enhanced testing protocols, vendor compliance assessments, employee training and certification, periodic audits and facility inspections.

Identified in the BRSR as a material risk covering hacking of websites and social media accounts, phishing attacks, drive-by downloads, insider threats, ransomware, insecure internet connectivity and unencrypted file sharing. Mitigated by not retaining sensitive customer financial details such as full card numbers, CVV or card expiry dates, strict access control to critical systems limited to authorised personnel, and advanced anti-virus and endpoint protection deployed across the organisation.

risks.risk: Underperformance and cash losses at the Indonesian subsidiary
risks.note: The Company assessed the recoverable value of its investment in PT Sari Burger Indonesia, which represents a separate cash generating unit, in view of cash losses incurred by the subsidiary and continued underperformance against revenue and other key financial performance indicators relative to its Annual Operating Plan; sensitivities applied to the discounted cash flow valuation led to an impairment provision being recorded for the year.

risks.risk: Sustained losses at the parent and absence of shareholder distributions
risks.note: The Company did not make a profit during the financial year, so no dividend is recommended and no amount is proposed to be transferred to reserves - constraining internal accrual funding for growth and leaving expansion dependent on external capital such as the QIP and the proposed capital infusion.

risks.risk: High employee attrition in a people-intensive format
risks.note: The turnover rate for permanent employees was 84.1 in FY 2025-26 (95.7 male, 64.6 female), improving from 97.06 in FY 2024-25 and 113.45 in FY 2023-24, but still elevated for a 12,372-strong workforce where service consistency depends on trained restaurant staff.

risks.risk: Customer service quality and complaint volume
risks.note: Customer complaints filed rose to 2,64,666 in FY 2025-26 from 1,16,249 in FY 2024-25, with the majority relating to ordering inaccuracies and food product experience; none were pending at the close of the year but the trend is a direct read on execution consistency and brand trust.

One hundred percent of the entity's turnover comes from Accommodation and Food Service activities, with food and beverage service activities (NIC Division 56) contributing 98.95% of turnover and exports contributing Nil, so results are fully exposed to Indian QSR demand and to the Indonesian operations held through subsidiaries.

Rising trade protectionism and higher US tariffs affected global trade while geopolitical tensions, including unrest in the Middle East and the Israel-Iran war, weighed on confidence; ongoing conflicts add pressure through higher commodity prices, rising inflation and increased financial stability risks, and India's export performance was affected following the conflict that began in late February 2026.

one-line thesis: RBA delivered a breakout Q4 with 6.3% SSSG (highest in 12 quarters) and 70% gross margins, driven by value-volume synergy and premium mix, though consolidated PAT is obscured by a one-time INR 120cr Indonesia impairment ahead of the Inspira Global acquisition.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,271cr FY26 (+~20% YoY implied); EBITDA: Company level 5.8% (FY26) vs 2.5% (FY23), Restaurant level 11.6%; PAT: Distorted by INR 120cr Indonesia impairment & INR 25cr Popeyes loss; Order Book: N/A (Organic store growth); Net Debt: Cash reduced to ~INR 190cr from INR 500cr due to capex and Indonesia infusion.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 60-80 net new stores/year; Margin: Targeting FCF neutral in 4-6 quarters (by FY28); Order Inflow: Steady dine-in traffic via 2for79/99; Capex: Heavy investment in electric broilers, solar, and Café rollout.
order book & pipeline: Net 68 stores added in FY26; Total count up >80% since FY22; Guidance maintained at 60-80 annual openings.
segment / subsidiary detail: India: SSSG 6.3% (Q4), 4% (FY26); Gross Margin 70.2% (Q4 exit); Digital orders 91%. Indonesia: BK turned positive on store EBITDA (IDR 8bn); Popeyes loss widened to IDR 25bn; Consolidated Indonesia negative EBITDA IDR 17bn.
growth verticals / optionality: BK Café targeting INR 25k ADS per store (long-term); Breakfast expansion with egg offerings; Premium 'King's Collection' driving APC; Digital CRM MAU up 51% YoY.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin expanded 320bps over 5 years (exit 70%); Drivers: Cluster strategy (local sourcing), product mix (premium burgers, high-margin cones/fizz), and utility savings (new electric broilers use 50% less energy).
capex / expansion: Focused on conversion to electric broilers (flame-grill retention), solar installations to offset LNG crisis, and Café equipment across all stores.
capital allocation: INR 20cr preferential infusion into Indonesia; Cash burn of ~INR 350cr opex + capex; Awaiting Inspira Global acquisition completion (CCI approval pending) for revised outlook.
risks & watch-items: Indonesia turnaround execution (Popeyes drag); LPG/LNG supply crisis impacting non-PNG stores; Integration risks with incoming promoter (Inspira Global/Lenexis); High cash burn before FCF neutrality.
management quality / tone: Confident on India momentum and margin discipline; Cautious but constructive on Indonesia BK turnaround; Definitive on exiting/fixing Popeyes; Transparent on one-time impairments.
non-obvious takeaways: The INR 120cr impairment is a 'big bath' before the Inspira deal closes, clearing the deck for new promoters; The shift to electric broilers is a strategic hedge against India's specific LNG volatility while maintaining brand essence (flame grill).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian food service market growth: valued at Rs 5,717 billion in FY 2025 and expected to reach Rs 9,688 billion by FY 2030 at a CAGR of 11.1% (Technopak)
- Shift from unorganised to organised formats: organised market share expected to rise from 50.1% in FY 2025 to around 60% by FY 2030, with the organised segment growing at a 15.2% CAGR
- Organised chain formats gaining share fastest - chain share of food services rising from 25% in FY 2020 to 32% in FY 2025 and an expected 36% by FY 2030P, at an 18.7% CAGR over FY 2025-30
- Digitalisation and food-delivery growth: smartphone and internet penetration make ordering more convenient, extending restaurant reach and adding revenue streams
- Structural global shift toward digital ordering and off-premise consumption, with cloud kitchens, AI-driven operations, sustainable packaging and plant-based menus reshaping food service
- Rising demand for diverse and global cuisines, encouraging menu diversification and international offerings
- Untapped potential in Tier II and III cities, where rising incomes and urban development are lifting demand for organised food services beyond metros
- Growing women workforce - female labour force participation up to 35.1% in January 2026 from 34.1% in April 2025 - and increasing nuclear families, driving convenience, ready-to-eat and eating-out demand
- Rising urbanisation - about 600 million urban residents expected by 2036 (about 40% of the population, contributing nearly 70% of GDP) - supporting expansion of branded food chains through malls, high streets and transit hubs
- Supportive demographics: over 65% of the population under age 35 as of February 2026, a young digitally connected cohort adopting delivery, digital payments and app-based discovery
- Favourable India macro backdrop: GDP growth estimated at 7.6% in FY 2025-26, repo rate cut by 125 basis points to 5.25%, and rising disposable incomes driving discretionary spending and premium experiences
- Indonesia macro support: economy grew 5.1% in 2025 and is expected to grow around 5.1% in 2026 with inflation easing to 2.6%, steady household spending and rising foreign reserves
- Headwinds flagged: rising real estate and rental costs in prime urban locations, still-low per capita spending on eating out in India, and external uncertainties and input cost pressures

The Company retains exclusive master franchise rights to develop, establish, operate and franchise Burger King restaurants in India, and through its Indonesian subsidiaries to develop Burger King and Popeyes in Indonesia, so future expansion runs through new restaurant development under a well-defined roll-out and development process supported by a vertically managed, scalable supply chain. On the funding side, the Company raised Rs 500 Crores through a Qualified Institutions Placement on March 26, 2025 with no deviation in the use of proceeds from the stated objects as on March 31, 2026, and enlarged its authorised share capital twice during the year - from Rs 600 crore to Rs 700 crore (AGM, August 21, 2025) and then to Rs 900 crore (EGM, February 13, 2026) - creating headroom for further issuance. moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Exclusive master franchise rights for the Burger King brand in India, and for Burger King and Popeyes in Indonesia through subsidiaries
- Leverage of a globally recognised brand present in over 125 markets with approximately 20,000 restaurants worldwide, plus its marketing, technical and operational expertise
- Strong customer proposition and brand positioning for millennials
- Vertically managed and scalable supply chain
- Operational quality, a people-centric operating culture and effective technology systems
- Well defined restaurant roll-out and development process that meets global brand standards
- Experienced and professional management team
- Digital-first operating model - 97% of restaurants equipped with self-ordering kiosks, table and app-based ordering in 100% of eligible restaurants and around 91% of sales through digital channels
- Barbell menu architecture spanning entry-level value, a strengthened core and a premium Kings Collection layer
- Twelve consecutive quarters of positive same-store traffic growth in the dine-in business

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Plastic waste is collected in line with the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) plan submitted to the Pollution Control Board, and the Company completed its EPR targets for the reporting period with the help of a third-party recycler.
- Waste oil generated at restaurants is disposed through designated vendors for production of bio-diesel and other approved by-products.
- E-waste from restaurant operations, corporate offices and IT infrastructure is disposed through authorised recyclers and vendors in compliance with e-waste management regulations, and paper waste is disposed safely through …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LNG shortage forcing kitchen fuel switches | Inox Wind / Siemens India | beneficiary | Low | RBA's aggressive shift to electric broilers and solar indicates a broader QSR trend toward electrification, benefiting industrial power equipment players. |
| Consolidated earnings drag from loss-making international subsidiary | Restaurant Brands Asia Ltd | loser | Med | Until the Inspira deal closes or Indonesia is fully restructured, consolidated PAT will remain volatile despite strong India operating performance. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Currency] Indonesia figures are translated at 1 Re = IDR 185 for Q1 FY27 versus 193 in Q1 FY26, so reported Indonesia INR trends carry a translation effect the deck flags in its footnotes.
- [Accounting] The deck's headline EBITDA measures are Pre IND AS-116 and are also stated Post Ind AS 116 in the summary tables; the Pre-IND AS 116 series excludes the impact of the new labor code in Q3 FY26 / FY26.
- [Name change] The company is presented as Restaurant Brands Asia Limited, formerly known as Burger King India Limited.
